I have resolved the issue where `Prefetch()` objects do not validate sliced querysets.

### Cause
When performing prefetching, Django filters the custom prefetch queryset with foreign keys matching the parent model instances. Attempting to filter a sliced queryset is disallowed and triggers a `TypeError("Cannot filter a query once a slice has been taken.")`. Previously, `Prefetch.__init__` did not validate if `queryset` was sliced, allowing sliced querysets to be passed and subsequently fail during evaluation.

### Solution
1. Updated [`Prefetch.__init__`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-saor7g81/django/db/models/query.py#L2148-L2158) in `django/db/models/query.py` to check `queryset.query.is_sliced` and raise `ValueError("Cannot filter a query once a slice has been taken.")` upon initialization.
2. Added test `test_sliced_queryset` in [`tests/prefetch_related/tests.py`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-saor7g81/tests/prefetch_related/tests.py#L1007-L1010) to verify `ValueError` is raised when passing a sliced queryset to `Prefetch`.
3. Updated documentation in [`docs/ref/models/querysets.txt`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-saor7g81/docs/ref/models/querysets.txt#L4010-L4013) to note that `Prefetch` custom querysets cannot use sliced querysets.
